Module 0: The Bridge from Word2Vec

From Static Semantic Dictionaries to Contextual State Spaces

Figure 0.1: Static Word2Vec Context Collapse vs. Dynamic Contextual Trajectories

0.1 Word2Vec's Polysemy Collapse

💡 Why?

  • Importance: Static word embedding models (such as Word2Vec and GloVe) enforce a bijective map between each discrete vocabulary token and a single static coordinate vector, forcing all senses and functions of a word into a single spatial coordinate.
  • Functional Role: Establishes the foundational motivation for the Transformer architecture: token representations must not be static parameters retrieved from disk, but dynamic runtime states that evolve as a function of the entire sequence context.
  • LLM Behavior Affected: If an LLM relied on static embeddings without context-dependent updates, it would suffer catastrophic polysemy collapse; words with diametrically opposed or domain-specific meanings (e.g., financial "bank" vs. geological "river bank") would project to identical vectors, rendering context-specific reasoning, translation, and ambiguity resolution impossible.

📖 Definition & Architecture

In the static embedding paradigm established by Mikolov et al. (2013a, 2013b), an embedding matrix assigns a static parameter vector e(w)∈Rd\mathbf{e}(w) \in \mathbb{R}^de(w)∈Rd to each word w∈Vw \in \mathcal{V}w∈V. This representation is context-free: whether the input sentence discusses agriculture, investment banking, or aeronautics, the vector coordinate remains invariant.

Natural language is fundamentally polysemous: a single lexical item www typically indexes a discrete set of latent senses S(w)={s1,s2,…,sK}\mathcal{S}(w) = \{s_1, s_2, \dots, s_K\}S(w)={s1​,s2​,…,sK​}. Because Word2Vec trains a single vector via Skip-Gram negative sampling or Continuous Bag of Words (CBOW) over a broad corpus, the resulting embedding collapses to a probability-weighted centroid of all its historical occurrences:

estatic(w)≈∑k=1KP(sk∣w)usk\mathbf{e}_{\text{static}}(w) \approx \sum_{k=1}^K P(s_k \mid w) \mathbf{u}_{s_k}estatic​(w)≈k=1∑K​P(sk​∣w)usk​​

where usk\mathbf{u}_{s_k}usk​​ denotes the ideal latent subspace representation of sense sks_ksk​. When two senses are orthogonal or contradictory, vector addition pulls the static embedding into an intermediate vacuum that accurately represents neither meaning.

The Transformer architecture solves this architectural bottleneck by decoupling the token identity from the contextual token state. While the network begins with a static lookup coordinate, successive Self-Attention layers calculate affinity scores across all surrounding tokens, dynamically shifting the vector along semantic trajectories.

![Figure 0.1: Static Word2Vec Context Collapse vs Dynamic Contextual Trajectory](assets/diagram_0_polysemy.jpg)

📐 The Mathematics & Working

In Word2Vec, the lookup function estatic:V→Rd\mathbf{e}_{\text{static}}: \mathcal{V} \to \mathbb{R}^destatic​:V→Rd satisfies:

estatic(w)=w∀ c∈C\mathbf{e}_{\text{static}}(w) = \mathbf{w} \quad \forall \, c \in \mathcal{C}estatic​(w)=w∀c∈C

In a Transformer, the contextualized representation hi(ℓ)∈Rdmodel\mathbf{h}_i^{(\ell)} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}}hi(ℓ)​∈Rdmodel​ at sequence position iii and layer ℓ\ellℓ is formulated as:

hi(0)=ei+pi\mathbf{h}_i^{(0)} = \mathbf{e}_i + \mathbf{p}_ihi(0)​=ei​+pi​
hi(ℓ)=hi(ℓ−1)+∑j=1Nαij(ℓ)(hj(ℓ−1)WV(ℓ))\mathbf{h}_i^{(\ell)} = \mathbf{h}_i^{(\ell-1)} + \sum_{j=1}^N \alpha_{ij}^{(\ell)} \left( \mathbf{h}_j^{(\ell-1)} W_V^{(\ell)} \right)hi(ℓ)​=hi(ℓ−1)​+j=1∑N​αij(ℓ)​(hj(ℓ−1)​WV(ℓ)​)
αij(ℓ)=exp⁡((hi(ℓ−1)WQ(ℓ))(hj(ℓ−1)WK(ℓ))⊤dk)∑m=1Nexp⁡((hi(ℓ−1)WQ(ℓ))(hm(ℓ−1)WK(ℓ))⊤dk)\alpha_{ij}^{(\ell)} = \frac{\exp\left( \frac{(\mathbf{h}_i^{(\ell-1)} W_Q^{(\ell)}) (\mathbf{h}_j^{(\ell-1)} W_K^{(\ell)})^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \right)}{\sum_{m=1}^N \exp\left( \frac{(\mathbf{h}_i^{(\ell-1)} W_Q^{(\ell)}) (\mathbf{h}_m^{(\ell-1)} W_K^{(\ell)})^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \right)}αij(ℓ)​=∑m=1N​exp(dk​​(hi(ℓ−1)​WQ(ℓ)​)(hm(ℓ−1)​WK(ℓ)​)⊤​)exp(dk​​(hi(ℓ−1)​WQ(ℓ)​)(hj(ℓ−1)​WK(ℓ)​)⊤​)​

  • V\mathcal{V}V: Discrete vocabulary set of size VVV.
  • C\mathcal{C}C: Set of all possible surrounding textual context windows.
  • w∈Rd\mathbf{w} \in \mathbb{R}^dw∈Rd: Static weight vector assigned to word www.
  • hi(ℓ)∈Rdmodel\mathbf{h}_i^{(\ell)} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}}hi(ℓ)​∈Rdmodel​: Contextualized activation vector of the token at position iii in layer ℓ\ellℓ.
  • ei∈Rdmodel\mathbf{e}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}}ei​∈Rdmodel​: Initial static token embedding retrieved from the embedding matrix.
  • pi∈Rdmodel\mathbf{p}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}}pi​∈Rdmodel​: Positional encoding vector injected at position iii.
  • NNN: Total number of tokens in the input context window.
  • αij(ℓ)∈R\alpha_{ij}^{(\ell)} \in \mathbb{R}αij(ℓ)​∈R: Scalar attention weight measuring the semantic relevance of token jjj to token iii at layer ℓ\ellℓ.
  • WQ(ℓ),WK(ℓ)∈Rdmodel×dkW_Q^{(\ell)}, W_K^{(\ell)} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}WQ(ℓ)​,WK(ℓ)​∈Rdmodel​×dk​: Query and Key projection parameter matrices at layer ℓ\ellℓ.
  • WV(ℓ)∈Rdmodel×dvW_V^{(\ell)} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_v}WV(ℓ)​∈Rdmodel​×dv​: Value projection parameter matrix at layer ℓ\ellℓ.
  • dk,dvd_k, d_vdk​,dv​: Dimensionality of the attention projection heads.

Word2Vec forces every word to occupy one unmoving coordinate in space, forcing conflicting meanings of a word to cancel each other out into a generic average. The Transformer uses attention weights to pull semantic information from neighboring words, dynamically steering the word's vector toward its exact situational meaning.

🌍 Real-World & NLP Behaviors

  • Financial vs. Ecological Disambiguation: In the sentence "The company had to bank on emergency federal credit after the river breached the northern bank", the token "bank" occurs twice with entirely distinct meanings. A static embedding model produces identical vectors for both instances, blinding downstream layers. A Transformer attends to "credit" and "federal" for the first occurrence, routing its representation into a finance-associated subspace, while attending to "river" and "breached" for the second, routing it into a geological/hydrological subspace.
  • Syntactic Category Shift (Noun vs. Verb Conversion): In "The complex houses married soldiers", the word "houses" acts as a transitive verb, and "complex" acts as an adjective modifying a noun phrase. Static models strongly bias "houses" toward its dominant noun centroid (residential buildings), frequently causing parse errors. A Transformer computes strong syntactic affinity between the subject noun phrase and the verb position, projecting "houses" into an action-predicate subspace that allows accurate causal and grammatical generation.

0.2 Token Embedding Matrix & The Residual Stream

💡 Why?

  • Importance: Digital hardware computes over continuous numerical tensors, whereas natural language consists of discrete, categorical tokens. The token embedding matrix defines the foundational coordinate mapping from discrete token IDs to the continuous geometric space where all representation learning occurs.
  • Functional Role: Instantiates the initial input vectors x0\mathbf{x}_0x0​ and establishes the Residual Stream—the shared communication bus running through every Transformer layer upon which self-attention heads and feed-forward networks perform additive read-and-write operations.
  • LLM Behavior Affected: Omission of a continuous embedding lookup makes gradient-based backpropagation impossible, as discrete tokens lack defined derivatives. Without preserving this vector space via an uncorrupted residual stream, deep layers overwrite or destroy earlier lexical information, causing catastrophic vanishing of prompt tokens across 32+ layers.

📖 Definition & Architecture

Let V\mathcal{V}V be a finite, ordered vocabulary of size VVV produced by a subword tokenizer (e.g., BPE, WordPiece). A discrete token is indexed by an integer t∈{0,1,…,V−1}t \in \{0, 1, \dots, V - 1\}t∈{0,1,…,V−1}. This discrete index can be represented as an indicator one-hot row vector t∈{0,1}V\mathbf{t} \in \{0, 1\}^Vt∈{0,1}V, where tk=1\mathbf{t}_k = 1tk​=1 if k=tk = tk=t and 000 otherwise.

The token embedding matrix WE∈RV×dmodelW_E \in \mathbb{R}^{V \times d_{\text{model}}}WE​∈RV×dmodel​ stores VVV distinct dmodeld_{\text{model}}dmodel​-dimensional learnable row vectors. Projecting a token ID into dense vector space is formulated as a linear matrix multiplication:

e=tWE\mathbf{e} = \mathbf{t} W_Ee=tWE​

In practice, machine learning frameworks optimize this sparse linear algebra into an O(1)\mathcal{O}(1)O(1) row-indexing operation: e=WE[t,:]\mathbf{e} = W_E[t, :]e=WE​[t,:].

Following Vaswani et al. (2017), the retrieved row vector is scaled by dmodel\sqrt{d_{\text{model}}}dmodel​​ prior to the injection of positional encodings. This scaling ensures that the expected Euclidean norm of the token representation matches downstream attention scaling and prevents the positional vector norm from dominating the lexical content:

xi(0)=dmodel⋅ei+pi\mathbf{x}_i^{(0)} = \sqrt{d_{\text{model}}} \cdot \mathbf{e}_i + \mathbf{p}_ixi(0)​=dmodel​​⋅ei​+pi​

As conceptualized by Elhage et al. (2021) in A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits, xi(0)\mathbf{x}_i^{(0)}xi(0)​ initializes the Residual Stream. Unlike classical sequential networks (e.g., LSTMs) where the hidden state is repeatedly transformed by non-linear matrix multiplications that warp coordinates at every step, the Transformer residual stream maintains a continuous linear highway:

xi(ℓ)=xi(ℓ−1)+Δxi,attn(ℓ)+Δxi,mlp(ℓ)\mathbf{x}_i^{(\ell)} = \mathbf{x}_i^{(\ell-1)} + \Delta \mathbf{x}_{i, \text{attn}}^{(\ell)} + \Delta \mathbf{x}_{i, \text{mlp}}^{(\ell)}xi(ℓ)​=xi(ℓ−1)​+Δxi,attn(ℓ)​+Δxi,mlp(ℓ)​

Layers communicate by reading from the stream via projection matrices and writing updates back via additive vector accumulation.

![Figure 0.2: Token Embedding Matrix Lookup and Residual Stream Projection](assets/diagram_0_2_embedding.jpg)

📐 The Mathematics & Working

The embedding lookup and initial residual stream injection are defined by:

ei=tiWE=WE[ti,:]\mathbf{e}_i = \mathbf{t}_i W_E = W_E[t_i, :]ei​=ti​WE​=WE​[ti​,:]
xi(0)=dmodel⋅ei+pi\mathbf{x}_i^{(0)} = \sqrt{d_{\text{model}}} \cdot \mathbf{e}_i + \mathbf{p}_ixi(0)​=dmodel​​⋅ei​+pi​

The propagation across LLL layers through the continuous residual stream is:

xi(ℓ)=xi(ℓ−1)+fattn(ℓ)(LN(x1:N(ℓ−1)))i+fMLP(ℓ)(LN(xi(ℓ−1),′))\mathbf{x}_i^{(\ell)} = \mathbf{x}_i^{(\ell-1)} + f_{\text{attn}}^{(\ell)}\left(\text{LN}(\mathbf{x}_{1:N}^{(\ell-1)})\right)_i + f_{\text{MLP}}^{(\ell)}\left(\text{LN}(\mathbf{x}_i^{(\ell-1), \prime})\right)xi(ℓ)​=xi(ℓ−1)​+fattn(ℓ)​(LN(x1:N(ℓ−1)​))i​+fMLP(ℓ)​(LN(xi(ℓ−1),′​))

where xi(ℓ−1),′=xi(ℓ−1)+fattn(ℓ)(LN(x1:N(ℓ−1)))i\mathbf{x}_i^{(\ell-1), \prime} = \mathbf{x}_i^{(\ell-1)} + f_{\text{attn}}^{(\ell)}\left(\text{LN}(\mathbf{x}_{1:N}^{(\ell-1)})\right)_ixi(ℓ−1),′​=xi(ℓ−1)​+fattn(ℓ)​(LN(x1:N(ℓ−1)​))i​.

  • VVV: Size of the tokenizer vocabulary (e.g., 32,000 to 128,256).
  • dmodeld_{\text{model}}dmodel​: Hidden state dimension of the Transformer (e.g., 4096 in LLaMA-3-8B).
  • WE∈RV×dmodelW_E \in \mathbb{R}^{V \times d_{\text{model}}}WE​∈RV×dmodel​: Learnable token embedding parameter matrix.
  • ti∈{0,…,V−1}t_i \in \{0, \dots, V-1\}ti​∈{0,…,V−1}: Discrete token integer ID at sequence position iii.
  • ti∈{0,1}V\mathbf{t}_i \in \{0, 1\}^Vti​∈{0,1}V: One-hot indicator vector corresponding to token ID tit_iti​.
  • ei∈Rdmodel\mathbf{e}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}}ei​∈Rdmodel​: Dense unscaled embedding vector for token iii.
  • pi∈Rdmodel\mathbf{p}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}}pi​∈Rdmodel​: Positional encoding vector injected at index iii.
  • xi(ℓ)∈Rdmodel\mathbf{x}_i^{(\ell)} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}}xi(ℓ)​∈Rdmodel​: Continuous residual stream activation vector at layer ℓ\ellℓ.
  • LN\text{LN}LN: Layer Normalization (or RMSNorm) operator.
  • fattn(ℓ)f_{\text{attn}}^{(\ell)}fattn(ℓ)​: Multi-head attention sub-layer at depth ℓ\ellℓ.
  • fMLP(ℓ)f_{\text{MLP}}^{(\ell)}fMLP(ℓ)​: Multi-layer perceptron (feed-forward) sub-layer at depth ℓ\ellℓ.
  • NNN: Total length of the input token sequence.

The token embedding matrix functions like an enormous dictionary that translates every discrete word ID into a high-dimensional spatial coordinate. This coordinate enters the residual stream, an additive vector highway that allows later attention and feed-forward layers to read the original token and add new layers of meaning without erasing the original word identity.

🌍 Real-World & NLP Behaviors

  • Subword Compositionality in BPE Tokenization: When encountering rare, technical, or neologistic terms like "unconstitutional", modern tokenizers split the string into subwords: ["un", "constitut", "ional"]. WEW_EWE​ maps each subword to an individual row vector. Because WEW_EWE​ is trained on billions of tokens, the vector for "un" occupies a direction corresponding to negation, while "ional" aligns with adjective formation. As these enter the residual stream, self-attention composes these disparate vectors into a unified lexical concept before semantic reasoning occurs.
  • Weight Tying with Output Unembedding (WU=WE⊤W_U = W_E^\topWU​=WE⊤​): In architectures utilizing weight tying (Press & Wolf, 2017), such as GPT-2 and Gemma, the input embedding matrix WEW_EWE​ is directly reused at the final layer as the unembedding matrix WU=WE⊤W_U = W_E^\topWU​=WE⊤​ to project the final residual state back into vocabulary logit space: z=x(L)WE⊤\mathbf{z} = \mathbf{x}^{(L)} W_E^\topz=x(L)WE⊤​. This geometric constraint enforces a strict duality: if two words share similar semantics, their input vectors must be close in Euclidean space, and a residual state pointing in that direction will assign high generation probability to both words simultaneously.

Module 1: Spatial & Order Foundations

Attention is Permutation-Invariant

1.1 Permutation Invariance of Set Operations

💡 Why?

  • Importance: The core mathematical operator of the Transformer—scaled dot-product attention—operates entirely on pairwise inner products and weighted sums, possessing zero intrinsic awareness of sequence order, temporal causality, or relative distance.
  • Functional Role: Formally exposes why Transformers, in their bare mathematical formulation, treat sequences as unordered bags of tokens (sets), proving why external positional signals are mathematically mandatory to model natural language syntax.
  • LLM Behavior Affected: If positional encodings were omitted, an LLM would compute identical representations for sentences containing identical words in different orders; "dog bites man" and "man bites dog" would yield the exact same multiset of hidden states, rendering grammatical parsing, temporal reasoning, code execution, and causal text generation completely non-functional.

📖 Definition & Architecture

In classical sequential neural architectures such as Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and LSTMs, sequential order is an architectural primitive:

ht=σ(Whht−1+Wxxt+b)\mathbf{h}_t = \sigma(W_h \mathbf{h}_{t-1} + W_x \mathbf{x}_t + \mathbf{b})ht​=σ(Wh​ht−1​+Wx​xt​+b)

The recurrent computation is strictly non-commutative because state ht\mathbf{h}_tht​ depends causally on its predecessor ht−1\mathbf{h}_{t-1}ht−1​.

In contrast, the Transformer processes all NNN tokens in parallel via matrix multiplication. Let X∈RN×dmodelX \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_{\text{model}}}X∈RN×dmodel​ denote the input matrix where row iii represents token vector xi\mathbf{x}_ixi​. The standard scaled dot-product attention mechanism is defined as:

Attn(X)=softmax((XWQ)(XWK)⊤dk)(XWV)\text{Attn}(X) = \text{softmax}\left( \frac{(X W_Q)(X W_K)^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \right) (X W_V)Attn(X)=softmax(dk​​(XWQ​)(XWK​)⊤​)(XWV​)

Let P∈{0,1}N×N\mathbf{P} \in \{0, 1\}^{N \times N}P∈{0,1}N×N be an arbitrary permutation matrix, defined such that PP⊤=I\mathbf{P} \mathbf{P}^\top = \mathbf{I}PP⊤=I and P1=1\mathbf{P} \mathbf{1} = \mathbf{1}P1=1. When the input sequence is permuted such that X~=PX\widetilde{X} = \mathbf{P} XX=PX, the queries, keys, and values undergo an identical row permutation:

Q~=PXWQ=PQ,K~=PXWK=PK,V~=PXWV=PV\widetilde{Q} = \mathbf{P} X W_Q = \mathbf{P} Q, \quad \widetilde{K} = \mathbf{P} X W_K = \mathbf{P} K, \quad \widetilde{V} = \mathbf{P} X W_V = \mathbf{P} VQ​=PXWQ​=PQ,K=PXWK​=PK,V=PXWV​=PV

Computing the attention weights yields:

A~=softmax(PQ(PK)⊤dk)=softmax(PQK⊤P⊤dk)=Psoftmax(QK⊤dk)P⊤=PAP⊤\widetilde{A} = \text{softmax}\left( \frac{\mathbf{P} Q (\mathbf{P} K)^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \right) = \text{softmax}\left( \frac{\mathbf{P} Q K^\top \mathbf{P}^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \right) = \mathbf{P} \text{softmax}\left( \frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \right) \mathbf{P}^\top = \mathbf{P} A \mathbf{P}^\topA=softmax(dk​​PQ(PK)⊤​)=softmax(dk​​PQK⊤P⊤​)=Psoftmax(dk​​QK⊤​)P⊤=PAP⊤

Multiplying by the values:

Attn(X~)=A~V~=(PAP⊤)(PV)=PA(P⊤P)V=P(AV)=PAttn(X)\text{Attn}(\widetilde{X}) = \widetilde{A} \widetilde{V} = (\mathbf{P} A \mathbf{P}^\top)(\mathbf{P} V) = \mathbf{P} A (\mathbf{P}^\top \mathbf{P}) V = \mathbf{P} (A V) = \mathbf{P} \text{Attn}(X)Attn(X)=AV=(PAP⊤)(PV)=PA(P⊤P)V=P(AV)=PAttn(X)

This mathematical equality proves that self-attention is strictly permutation equivariant: permuting the input sequence merely permutes the corresponding rows of the output matrix without altering any interaction score. If the output rows are pooled or compared independently of row order, the operation is permutation invariant. Without an injected positional signal, the network cannot distinguish where a word appears in time or space.

![Figure 1.1: Recurrent Sequential Processing vs Transformer Permutation Invariance](assets/diagram_1_1_permutation.jpg)

📐 The Mathematics & Working

The permutation equivariance condition for self-attention is formally stated as:

Attn(PX)=P⋅Attn(X)∀ P∈PN\text{Attn}(\mathbf{P} X) = \mathbf{P} \cdot \text{Attn}(X) \quad \forall \, \mathbf{P} \in \mathcal{P}_NAttn(PX)=P⋅Attn(X)∀P∈PN​

where the attention operator is:

Attn(X)=softmax(XWQWK⊤X⊤dk)XWV\text{Attn}(X) = \text{softmax}\left( \frac{X W_Q W_K^\top X^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \right) X W_VAttn(X)=softmax(dk​​XWQ​WK⊤​X⊤​)XWV​

  • X∈RN×dmodelX \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_{\text{model}}}X∈RN×dmodel​: Input sequence activation matrix containing NNN token vectors.
  • NNN: Sequence length (number of tokens).
  • dmodeld_{\text{model}}dmodel​: Channel dimension of the hidden representation.
  • PN\mathcal{P}_NPN​: Set of all N×NN \times NN×N permutation matrices.
  • P∈PN\mathbf{P} \in \mathcal{P}_NP∈PN​: Binary orthogonal matrix containing exactly one 1 in each row and column.
  • WQ,WK∈Rdmodel×dkW_Q, W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}WQ​,WK​∈Rdmodel​×dk​: Linear projection matrices mapping tokens to Query and Key spaces.
  • WV∈Rdmodel×dvW_V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_v}WV​∈Rdmodel​×dv​: Linear projection matrix mapping tokens to Value space.
  • dkd_kdk​: Dimensional scaling factor preventing dot products from growing excessively large in high dimensions.
  • softmax(⋅)\text{softmax}(\cdot)softmax(⋅): Row-wise normalized exponential function.

Raw self-attention computes connections between words purely by comparing their content, treating an entire paragraph like an unordered collection of tiles dumped out of a box. Because rearranging the tiles simply scrambles the rows of the final answer without changing any internal calculation, the model cannot tell the difference between words that are side-by-side and words that are miles apart.

🌍 Real-World & NLP Behaviors

  • Agent-Patient Inversion in Semantic Parsing: Consider the sentences "The cat hunted the mouse" versus "The mouse hunted the cat". Both sentences contain the identical bag of words: {"The", "cat", "hunted", "the", "mouse"}. Without an explicit positional signal, the unpermuted attention scores between "hunted" and "cat" are mathematically identical in both cases. The model cannot identify whether "cat" is the agent (predator) or the patient (prey), causing catastrophic failures in question answering and semantic role labeling.
  • Assignment Logic in Source Code Generation: In programming languages, order dictates dataflow. The statement x = y assigns the value of variable y into x, whereas y = x assigns x into y. Without positional awareness, an attention layer computes identical self-attention affinities between the variable names and the assignment operator = regardless of token position, making it impossible for a code-generation LLM to maintain variable scope or write syntactically correct software.

1.2 Absolute Sinusoidal Positional Encoding

💡 Why?

  • Importance: Vaswani et al. (2017) introduced absolute sinusoidal positional encodings to inject deterministic, zero-parameter sequential order directly into the Transformer architecture, breaking permutation invariance without requiring learned lookup tables.
  • Functional Role: Adds a unique, continuous, high-dimensional coordinate vector to each token embedding prior to layer 0, encoding both absolute sequence position (pospospos) and enabling linear transformations to represent relative offsets (pos+kpos + kpos+k).
  • LLM Behavior Affected: Enables the model to attend to tokens based on their position in the sequence (e.g., attending to the immediate previous token, the first token of a sentence, or a delimiter). If omitted, the model cannot distinguish between sequences with identical word distributions; if implemented with insufficient frequency resolution, the model fails to track distance and degrades over long context spans.

📖 Definition & Architecture

Vaswani et al. (2017) recognized that an ideal positional encoding scheme must satisfy three criteria:

1. It must output a unique vector ppos\mathbf{p}_{pos}ppos​ for every integer position pos∈[0,N−1]pos \in [0, N-1]pos∈[0,N−1].

2. The distance between positions pospospos and pos+kpos + kpos+k must be consistent regardless of absolute position pospospos.

3. The function must generalize to sequence lengths longer than those observed during training.

To achieve this, the authors defined Sinusoidal Positional Encoding using a geometric progression of sinusoidal frequencies across the hidden dimension indices. For a token at index pospospos and dimension channel 2i2i2i (even) and 2i+12i + 12i+1 (odd):

PE(pos,2i)=sin⁡(pos100002i/dmodel)PE_{(pos, 2i)} = \sin\left( \frac{pos}{10000^{2i / d_{\text{model}}}} \right)PE(pos,2i)​=sin(100002i/dmodel​pos​)
PE(pos,2i+1)=cos⁡(pos100002i/dmodel)PE_{(pos, 2i+1)} = \cos\left( \frac{pos}{10000^{2i / d_{\text{model}}}} \right)PE(pos,2i+1)​=cos(100002i/dmodel​pos​)

where i∈{0,1,…,dmodel2−1}i \in \{0, 1, \dots, \frac{d_{\text{model}}}{2} - 1\}i∈{0,1,…,2dmodel​​−1}.

The angular frequency for dimension pair iii is defined as:

ωi=1100002i/dmodel\omega_i = \frac{1}{10000^{2i / d_{\text{model}}}}ωi​=100002i/dmodel​1​

The corresponding wavelength λi=2πωi=2π⋅100002i/dmodel\lambda_i = \frac{2\pi}{\omega_i} = 2\pi \cdot 10000^{2i / d_{\text{model}}}λi​=ωi​2π​=2π⋅100002i/dmodel​ forms a geometric progression:

  • At channel i=0i = 0i=0: λ0=2π≈6.28\lambda_0 = 2\pi \approx 6.28λ0​=2π≈6.28 tokens (ultra-high frequency, tracking fine-grained adjacent token transitions).
  • At channel i=dmodel2−1i = \frac{d_{\text{model}}}{2} - 1i=2dmodel​​−1: λ≈20000π≈62,831\lambda \approx 20000\pi \approx 62,831λ≈20000π≈62,831 tokens (ultra-low frequency, tracking broad macro-structural document pacing).

A crucial mathematical property of this formulation is the Linear Shift Property: for any fixed offset kkk, PEpos+kPE_{pos + k}PEpos+k​ can be computed as a direct linear transformation of PEposPE_{pos}PEpos​. Using standard trigonometric addition theorems:

sin⁡(ωi(pos+k))=sin⁡(ωipos)cos⁡(ωik)+cos⁡(ωipos)sin⁡(ωik)\sin(\omega_i(pos + k)) = \sin(\omega_i pos)\cos(\omega_i k) + \cos(\omega_i pos)\sin(\omega_i k)sin(ωi​(pos+k))=sin(ωi​pos)cos(ωi​k)+cos(ωi​pos)sin(ωi​k)
cos⁡(ωi(pos+k))=cos⁡(ωipos)cos⁡(ωik)−sin⁡(ωipos)sin⁡(ωik)\cos(\omega_i(pos + k)) = \cos(\omega_i pos)\cos(\omega_i k) - \sin(\omega_i pos)\sin(\omega_i k)cos(ωi​(pos+k))=cos(ωi​pos)cos(ωi​k)−sin(ωi​pos)sin(ωi​k)

In matrix form, the 2D subspace corresponding to frequency channel iii undergoes an orthogonal rotation by angle ωik\omega_i kωi​k:

[PE(pos+k,2i)PE(pos+k,2i+1)]=[cos⁡(ωik)sin⁡(ωik)−sin⁡(ωik)cos⁡(ωik)][PE(pos,2i)PE(pos,2i+1)]\begin{bmatrix} PE_{(pos+k, 2i)} \\ PE_{(pos+k, 2i+1)} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos(\omega_i k) & \sin(\omega_i k) \\ -\sin(\omega_i k) & \cos(\omega_i k) \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} PE_{(pos, 2i)} \\ PE_{(pos, 2i+1)} \end{bmatrix}[PE(pos+k,2i)​PE(pos+k,2i+1)​​]=[cos(ωi​k)−sin(ωi​k)​sin(ωi​k)cos(ωi​k)​][PE(pos,2i)​PE(pos,2i+1)​​]

This guarantees that the self-attention mechanism can learn to attend by relative position using simple bilinear projections.

![Figure 1.2: Frequency Spectrum of Sinusoidal Positional Encoding](assets/diagram_1_2_sinusoidal.jpg)

📐 The Mathematics & Working

The absolute sinusoidal positional encoding vector PEpos∈RdmodelPE_{pos} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}}PEpos​∈Rdmodel​ is defined element-wise by:

PE(pos,2i)=sin⁡(ωi⋅pos),PE(pos,2i+1)=cos⁡(ωi⋅pos)PE_{(pos, 2i)} = \sin(\omega_i \cdot pos), \quad PE_{(pos, 2i+1)} = \cos(\omega_i \cdot pos)PE(pos,2i)​=sin(ωi​⋅pos),PE(pos,2i+1)​=cos(ωi​⋅pos)

where the frequency parameter is:

ωi=10000−2idmodel\omega_i = 10000^{-\frac{2i}{d_{\text{model}}}}ωi​=10000−dmodel​2i​

The relative shift operator is given by the block-diagonal linear transformation:

ppos+k=Mkppos\mathbf{p}_{pos+k} = M_k \mathbf{p}_{pos}ppos+k​=Mk​ppos​

where Mk∈Rdmodel×dmodelM_k \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_{\text{model}}}Mk​∈Rdmodel​×dmodel​ is a block-diagonal matrix composed of 2×22 \times 22×2 rotation blocks:

Mk(i)=[cos⁡(ωik)sin⁡(ωik)−sin⁡(ωik)cos⁡(ωik)]M_k^{(i)} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos(\omega_i k) & \sin(\omega_i k) \\ -\sin(\omega_i k) & \cos(\omega_i k) \end{bmatrix}Mk(i)​=[cos(ωi​k)−sin(ωi​k)​sin(ωi​k)cos(ωi​k)​]
  • pos∈{0,1,…,N−1}pos \in \{0, 1, \dots, N-1\}pos∈{0,1,…,N−1}: Discrete sequence index of the token.
  • i∈{0,1,…,dmodel2−1}i \in \{0, 1, \dots, \frac{d_{\text{model}}}{2} - 1\}i∈{0,1,…,2dmodel​​−1}: Index of the frequency sub-channel.
  • 2i,2i+12i, 2i+12i,2i+1: Even and odd coordinate indices within the dmodeld_{\text{model}}dmodel​-dimensional vector.
  • dmodeld_{\text{model}}dmodel​: Total dimensionality of the model hidden state.
  • ωi∈R\omega_i \in \mathbb{R}ωi​∈R: Angular frequency associated with channel iii.
  • k∈Zk \in \mathbb{Z}k∈Z: Integer positional displacement between two tokens.
  • Mk∈Rdmodel×dmodelM_k \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_{\text{model}}}Mk​∈Rdmodel​×dmodel​: Block-diagonal orthogonal transformation matrix encoding relative offset kkk.
  • ppos∈Rdmodel\mathbf{p}_{pos} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}}ppos​∈Rdmodel​: Full positional encoding vector injected at sequence position pospospos.

Sinusoidal encoding gives each word position a unique mathematical signature built from dozens of overlapping sine and cosine waves running from fast ripples to slow ocean swells. Because these waves obey exact rotation formulas, the network can easily calculate the distance between any two words simply by taking their dot product.

🌍 Real-World & NLP Behaviors

  • Local Syntactic Agreement vs. Global Discourse Tracking: In German or Russian, case markers and adjective-noun agreements occur within short distances (1–3 tokens), whereas verb clauses in subordinate sentences can be separated by dozens of tokens. Sinusoidal encoding enables the model to allocate high-frequency dimensions (where λ\lambdaλ is small) to track local syntactic dependencies (e.g., immediate modifier-noun agreement) while low-frequency dimensions preserve absolute chapter-level or paragraph-level narrative pacing without aliasing.
  • Failure in Length Extrapolation (The Absolute Position Barrier): When early models trained with absolute sinusoidal encodings (like original Transformer-Base or learned absolute embeddings in GPT-3) were evaluated on sequences longer than their training window (e.g., evaluating on 4096 tokens after training on 2048), performance collapsed catastrophically. The query-key dot products at positions pos>2048pos > 2048pos>2048 generated vector values outside the training manifold, causing attention logits to blow up and demonstrating that simply adding absolute coordinates directly into token embeddings pollutes semantic representations at scale.
Figure 1.3: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) — 2D Complex Subspace Rotation & Relative Distance Angle (m - n)θ

1.3 Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE)

💡 Why?

  • Importance: Rotary Position Embedding (Su et al., 2021) is the dominant positional mechanism across modern frontier and open-weight architectures (LLaMA 1/2/3, Mistral, Qwen, Gemma 2, DeepSeek-V2/V3). It resolves the core flaw of absolute positional addition by implementing relative positional encoding through complex orthogonal rotations.
  • Functional Role: Instead of adding positional vectors to token embeddings in the residual stream, RoPE rotates the projected Query (q\mathbf{q}q) and Key (k\mathbf{k}k) vectors in 2D coordinate sub-planes prior to the attention dot-product, ensuring the resulting inner product ⟨Rmq,Rnk⟩\langle R_m \mathbf{q}, R_n \mathbf{k} \rangle⟨Rm​q,Rn​k⟩ is a function strictly of the relative distance (m−n)(m - n)(m−n).
  • LLM Behavior Affected: Preserves the L2L_2L2​ norm of Query and Key vectors (since rotation is an orthogonal isometric transformation), eliminates positional noise pollution from the residual stream, induces a natural decay of attention weights over distance via the Riemann-Lebesgue lemma, and enables context-window extension to hundreds of thousands of tokens via frequency interpolation.

📖 Definition & Architecture

In absolute additive encoding, adding pm\mathbf{p}_mpm​ and pn\mathbf{p}_npn​ to the input vectors expands the query-key dot product into four entangled terms:

qm⊤kn=(xm+pm)WQWK⊤(xn+pn)⊤=xmWQWK⊤xn⊤+xmWQWK⊤pn⊤+pmWQWK⊤xn⊤+pmWQWK⊤pn⊤\mathbf{q}_m^\top \mathbf{k}_n = (\mathbf{x}_m + \mathbf{p}_m) W_Q W_K^\top (\mathbf{x}_n + \mathbf{p}_n)^\top = \mathbf{x}_m W_Q W_K^\top \mathbf{x}_n^\top + \mathbf{x}_m W_Q W_K^\top \mathbf{p}_n^\top + \mathbf{p}_m W_Q W_K^\top \mathbf{x}_n^\top + \mathbf{p}_m W_Q W_K^\top \mathbf{p}_n^\topqm⊤​kn​=(xm​+pm​)WQ​WK⊤​(xn​+pn​)⊤=xm​WQ​WK⊤​xn⊤​+xm​WQ​WK⊤​pn⊤​+pm​WQ​WK⊤​xn⊤​+pm​WQ​WK⊤​pn⊤​

This entangles semantic content with positional coordinates, forcing the network to waste capacity disentangling cross-terms.

Su et al. (2021) formulated RoFormer by seeking an operation that injects positional coordinates into Query qm\mathbf{q}_mqm​ and Key kn\mathbf{k}_nkn​ such that their inner product depends exclusively on the relative displacement m−nm - nm−n:

⟨fq(xm,m),fk(xn,n)⟩=g(xm,xn,m−n)\langle f_q(\mathbf{x}_m, m), f_k(\mathbf{x}_n, n) \rangle = g(\mathbf{x}_m, \mathbf{x}_n, m - n)⟨fq​(xm​,m),fk​(xn​,n)⟩=g(xm​,xn​,m−n)

By framing the problem over the 2D plane and leveraging complex numbers, Euler's formula provides a natural solution. Let a 2D vector x=[x1,x2]⊤\mathbf{x} = [x_1, x_2]^\topx=[x1​,x2​]⊤ be represented as a complex number z=x1+ix2z = x_1 + i x_2z=x1​+ix2​. Rotating zzz by an angle proportional to position mmm is equivalent to multiplying by eimθe^{i m \theta}eimθ:

Rθ,mz=(x1+ix2)eimθ=(x1cos⁡(mθ)−x2sin⁡(mθ))+i(x1sin⁡(mθ)+x2cos⁡(mθ))R_{\theta, m} z = (x_1 + i x_2) e^{i m \theta} = (x_1 \cos(m\theta) - x_2 \sin(m\theta)) + i (x_1 \sin(m\theta) + x_2 \cos(m\theta))Rθ,m​z=(x1​+ix2​)eimθ=(x1​cos(mθ)−x2​sin(mθ))+i(x1​sin(mθ)+x2​cos(mθ))

In real matrix form, this corresponds to the 2×22 \times 22×2 orthogonal rotation matrix:

Rθ,m=[cos⁡(mθ)−sin⁡(mθ)sin⁡(mθ)cos⁡(mθ)]R_{\theta, m} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos(m\theta) & -\sin(m\theta) \\ \sin(m\theta) & \cos(m\theta) \end{bmatrix}Rθ,m​=[cos(mθ)sin(mθ)​−sin(mθ)cos(mθ)​]

For a ddd-dimensional space (where ddd is the head dimension dkd_kdk​), the vector is partitioned into d/2d/2d/2 independent two-dimensional sub-planes. Each pair of dimensions (2i,2i+1)(2i, 2i+1)(2i,2i+1) is assigned a distinct base frequency θi=b−2(i−1)/d\theta_i = b^{-2(i-1)/d}θi​=b−2(i−1)/d, where bbb is the base (typically 10,000, or 500,000 in LLaMA-3). The full transformation matrix RΘ,md\mathbf{R}_{\Theta, m}^dRΘ,md​ is a block-diagonal orthogonal matrix:

RΘ,md=diag(Rθ1,m,Rθ2,m,…,Rθd/2,m)\mathbf{R}_{\Theta, m}^d = \text{diag}\left( R_{\theta_1, m}, R_{\theta_2, m}, \dots, R_{\theta_{d/2}, m} \right)RΘ,md​=diag(Rθ1​,m​,Rθ2​,m​,…,Rθd/2​,m​)

When computing the self-attention score between query at position mmm and key at position nnn:

⟨RΘ,mdqm,RΘ,ndkn⟩=(RΘ,mdqm)⊤(RΘ,ndkn)=qm⊤(RΘ,md)⊤RΘ,ndkn\langle \mathbf{R}_{\Theta, m}^d \mathbf{q}_m, \mathbf{R}_{\Theta, n}^d \mathbf{k}_n \rangle = (\mathbf{R}_{\Theta, m}^d \mathbf{q}_m)^\top (\mathbf{R}_{\Theta, n}^d \mathbf{k}_n) = \mathbf{q}_m^\top (\mathbf{R}_{\Theta, m}^d)^\top \mathbf{R}_{\Theta, n}^d \mathbf{k}_n⟨RΘ,md​qm​,RΘ,nd​kn​⟩=(RΘ,md​qm​)⊤(RΘ,nd​kn​)=qm⊤​(RΘ,md​)⊤RΘ,nd​kn​

Because rotation matrices form an abelian group under addition, (RΘ,md)⊤=RΘ,−md(\mathbf{R}_{\Theta, m}^d)^\top = \mathbf{R}_{\Theta, -m}^d(RΘ,md​)⊤=RΘ,−md​, which gives:

(RΘ,md)⊤RΘ,nd=RΘ,−mdRΘ,nd=RΘ,n−md(\mathbf{R}_{\Theta, m}^d)^\top \mathbf{R}_{\Theta, n}^d = \mathbf{R}_{\Theta, -m}^d \mathbf{R}_{\Theta, n}^d = \mathbf{R}_{\Theta, n - m}^d(RΘ,md​)⊤RΘ,nd​=RΘ,−md​RΘ,nd​=RΘ,n−md​

Thus:

⟨RΘ,mdqm,RΘ,ndkn⟩=qm⊤RΘ,n−mdkn\langle \mathbf{R}_{\Theta, m}^d \mathbf{q}_m, \mathbf{R}_{\Theta, n}^d \mathbf{k}_n \rangle = \mathbf{q}_m^\top \mathbf{R}_{\Theta, n - m}^d \mathbf{k}_n⟨RΘ,md​qm​,RΘ,nd​kn​⟩=qm⊤​RΘ,n−md​kn​

The dot product depends purely on the relative distance n−mn - mn−m. Furthermore, RoPE is applied only to Query and Key projections; Value vectors (v\mathbf{v}v) and the residual stream remain completely untouched.

📐 The Mathematics & Working

The rotary transformation applied to query vector qm∈Rdk\mathbf{q}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k}qm​∈Rdk​ and key vector kn∈Rdk\mathbf{k}_n \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k}kn​∈Rdk​ is:

q~m=RΘ,mdqm,k~n=RΘ,ndkn\widetilde{\mathbf{q}}_m = \mathbf{R}_{\Theta, m}^d \mathbf{q}_m, \quad \widetilde{\mathbf{k}}_n = \mathbf{R}_{\Theta, n}^d \mathbf{k}_nq​m​=RΘ,md​qm​,kn​=RΘ,nd​kn​

where RΘ,md∈Rdk×dk\mathbf{R}_{\Theta, m}^d \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k \times d_k}RΘ,md​∈Rdk​×dk​ is defined as:

RΘ,md=[cos⁡(mθ1)−sin⁡(mθ1)00⋯00sin⁡(mθ1)cos⁡(mθ1)00⋯0000cos⁡(mθ2)−sin⁡(mθ2)⋯0000sin⁡(mθ2)cos⁡(mθ2)⋯00⋮⋮⋮⋮⋱⋮⋮0000⋯cos⁡(mθdk/2)−sin⁡(mθdk/2)0000⋯sin⁡(mθdk/2)cos⁡(mθdk/2)]\mathbf{R}_{\Theta, m}^d = \begin{bmatrix}

\cos(m\theta_1) & -\sin(m\theta_1) & 0 & 0 & \cdots & 0 & 0 \\

\sin(m\theta_1) & \cos(m\theta_1) & 0 & 0 & \cdots & 0 & 0 \\

0 & 0 & \cos(m\theta_2) & -\sin(m\theta_2) & \cdots & 0 & 0 \\

\vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots & \vdots \\

0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots & \cos(m\theta_{d_k/2}) & -\sin(m\theta_{d_k/2}) \\

0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots & \sin(m\theta_{d_k/2}) & \cos(m\theta_{d_k/2})

\end{bmatrix}RΘ,md​=​cos(mθ1​)sin(mθ1​)00⋮00​−sin(mθ1​)cos(mθ1​)00⋮00​00cos(mθ2​)sin(mθ2​)⋮00​00−sin(mθ2​)cos(mθ2​)⋮00​⋯⋯⋯⋯⋱⋯⋯​0000⋮cos(mθdk​/2​)sin(mθdk​/2​)​0000⋮−sin(mθdk​/2​)cos(mθdk​/2​)​​

with frequency scale:

θi=b−2(i−1)dk,i∈{1,2,…,dk2}\theta_i = b^{-\frac{2(i-1)}{d_k}}, \quad i \in \left\{1, 2, \dots, \frac{d_k}{2}\right\}θi​=b−dk​2(i−1)​,i∈{1,2,…,2dk​​}

The relative attention dot product is:

q~m⊤k~n=qm⊤RΘ,n−mdkn\widetilde{\mathbf{q}}_m^\top \widetilde{\mathbf{k}}_n = \mathbf{q}_m^\top \mathbf{R}_{\Theta, n - m}^d \mathbf{k}_nq​m⊤​kn​=qm⊤​RΘ,n−md​kn​

  • qm∈Rdk\mathbf{q}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k}qm​∈Rdk​: Query vector produced at sequence position mmm by linear projection xmWQ\mathbf{x}_m W_Qxm​WQ​.
  • kn∈Rdk\mathbf{k}_n \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k}kn​∈Rdk​: Key vector produced at sequence position nnn by linear projection xnWK\mathbf{x}_n W_Kxn​WK​.
  • m,n∈{0,1,…,N−1}m, n \in \{0, 1, \dots, N-1\}m,n∈{0,1,…,N−1}: Discrete sequence positions of the query and key tokens.
  • m−n∈Zm - n \in \mathbb{Z}m−n∈Z: Relative displacement between query token and key token.
  • dkd_kdk​: Channel dimension of an individual attention head.
  • iii: Index of the 2D rotary sub-plane (1≤i≤dk/21 \le i \le d_k / 21≤i≤dk​/2).
  • θi\theta_iθi​: Frequency assigned to the iii-th sub-plane.
  • bbb: Frequency base hyperparameter (b=10,000b = 10,000b=10,000 in standard RoFormer/LLaMA-1; b=500,000b = 500,000b=500,000 in LLaMA-3).
  • RΘ,md\mathbf{R}_{\Theta, m}^dRΘ,md​: Orthogonal block-diagonal matrix rotating each coordinate pair by angle mθim\theta_imθi​.
  • q~m,k~n\widetilde{\mathbf{q}}_m, \widetilde{\mathbf{k}}_nq​m​,kn​: Position-rotated query and key vectors fed into the scaled dot-product attention kernel.

    RoPE twists every pair of dimensions in the query and key vectors by an angle proportional to their position along the sentence before comparing them. Because the dot product of two rotated vectors depends only on the difference between their rotation angles, the attention score measures the exact relative distance between the words while keeping their vector lengths completely unchanged.

🌍 Real-World & NLP Behaviors

  • Needle In A Haystack (NIAH) Long-Context Retrieval: In long-context evaluations (e.g., retrieving a single sentence hidden inside a 128,000-token document), models with additive positional encodings suffer severe degradation because distant tokens produce high-variance positional noise that drowns out the needle. RoPE naturally attenuates attention weights as ∣m−n∣|m - n|∣m−n∣ increases (long-term decay) while allowing the model to sharply match queries and keys across huge offsets via frequency alignment, enabling models like LLaMA-3 and Qwen-2 to achieve 100% retrieval accuracy across 128k context windows.
  • Context Extension via RoPE Frequency Scaling (YaRN & RoPE Base Scaling): When scaling LLaMA from its native 4k context window to 32k or 128k tokens, unseen positions m>4096m > 4096m>4096 generate out-of-distribution rotation angles in high-frequency dimensions. Instead of full retraining, practitioners apply RoPE scaling (such as Linear Interpolation or YaRN): they decrease the base frequencies θi\theta_iθi​ by scaling factor sss (e.g., θi′=θi/s\theta_i' = \theta_i / sθi′​=θi​/s or adjusting the base bbb from 10,000 to 500,000). Because RoPE's relative geometry is continuous, the network interprets a 128k context as if it were a high-density 4k context, extending sequence capacity with minimal fine-tuning compute.

Module 2: Self-Attention Dissected (The Core Router)

Self-attention is the fundamental routing primitive of the Transformer architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017). Unlike static recurrent units or local convolutional receptive fields, self-attention constructs dynamic, data-dependent connectivity graphs across all sequence positions simultaneously. In this module, we dissect the mathematical mechanics of the scaled dot-product attention engine into five constituent atomic stages.

2.1 The Three Projections (WQ,WK,WVW_Q, W_K, W_VWQ​,WK​,WV​)

💡 Why?

  • Decoupled Functional Roles: In natural language, a token's identity as a searcher (what it is looking for), as an indexable target (what properties it advertises to others), and as an informational payload (what semantic content it actually transmits) are distinct semantic concepts. A single static embedding vector cannot simultaneously serve all three functional objectives without catastrophic representational interference.
  • Architectural Role: The projection matrices WQ,WK,WV∈Rdmodel×dkW_Q, W_K, W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}WQ​,WK​,WV​∈Rdmodel​×dk​ (or dvd_vdv​) linearly project raw token representations into three specialized representational geometric subspaces: Queries (QQQ), Keys (KKK), and Values (VVV).
  • Failure Mode Without Projections: If an architecture computes attention directly on raw embeddings XXX as XXTXX X^T XXXTX, the affinity matrix is symmetric along the diagonal and strictly dominated by vector magnitude and static lexical similarity. The model loses asymmetric routing (e.g., a verb seeking its direct object cannot distinguish its search query from its advertised key), collapsing directional grammar and syntactic role assignment.

📖 Definition & Architecture

Vaswani et al. (2017) formalized attention as mapping a query and a set of key-value pairs to an output. Given an input sequence matrix X∈RN×dmodelX \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_{\text{model}}}X∈RN×dmodel​, where NNN denotes sequence length and dmodeld_{\text{model}}dmodel​ is the residual stream dimension, the model learns three separate weight parameter matrices:

1. Query Matrix (WQW_QWQ​): Projects XXX into queries QQQ, representing the informational deficit or search profile of each token position.

2. Key Matrix (WKW_KWK​): Projects XXX into keys KKK, representing the addressable semantic catalog of each token position.

3. Value Matrix (WVW_VWV​): Projects XXX into values VVV, containing the substantive semantic payload extracted if a key is successfully matched.

![Figure 2.1: Query, Key, and Value Linear Projections](assets/diagram_2_1_projections.jpg)

Input Matrix X [N × d_model]

W_Q [d_model × d_k]

W_K [d_model × d_k]

W_V [d_model × d_v]

Queries Q = X · W_Q

Keys K = X · W_K

Values V = X · W_V

📐 The Mathematics & Working

The projections are linear affine mappings without bias terms (in modern standard LLMs such as LLaMA and Mistral):

Q=XWQQ = X W_QQ=XWQ​
K=XWKK = X W_KK=XWK​
V=XWVV = X W_VV=XWV​
  • X∈RN×dmodelX \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_{\text{model}}}X∈RN×dmodel​: Input matrix containing NNN token sequence vectors of dimensionality dmodeld_{\text{model}}dmodel​.
  • WQ∈Rdmodel×dkW_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}WQ​∈Rdmodel​×dk​: Query projection parameter weight matrix.
  • WK∈Rdmodel×dkW_K \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}WK​∈Rdmodel​×dk​: Key projection parameter weight matrix.
  • WV∈Rdmodel×dvW_V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_v}WV​∈Rdmodel​×dv​: Value projection parameter weight matrix (typically dk=dv=dmodel/hd_k = d_v = d_{\text{model}} / hdk​=dv​=dmodel​/h).
  • Q∈RN×dkQ \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_k}Q∈RN×dk​: Query matrix where row iii represents query vector qiq_iqi​.
  • K∈RN×dkK \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_k}K∈RN×dk​: Key matrix where row jjj represents key vector kjk_jkj​.
  • V∈RN×dvV \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_v}V∈RN×dv​: Value matrix where row jjj represents value vector vjv_jvj​.

2-Sentence Plain Lingo:

The three projections transform each token vector into three separate roles: an inquiry asking what information is needed, an address tag announcing what information is present, and a content payload containing the actual message. By separating these roles through distinct learned matrices, a word can search for one specific grammatical relation without being forced to broadcast that same relationship as its own identity.

🌍 Real-World & NLP Behaviors

  • Example 1: Asymmetric Subject-Verb Routing: In "The chef who prepared the dishes was exhausted", the singular verb "was" must resolve its long-distance grammatical agreement with "chef" rather than the plural noun "dishes". Through WQW_QWQ​, "was" emits a query seeking a singular syntactic head subject, while "chef" emits a key via WKW_KWK​ matching that search criteria; the value payload VVV from "chef" transfers the singular semantic agreement feature into "was".
  • Example 2: Anaphora / Coreference Resolution: In "The trophy didn't fit into the brown suitcase because it was too large", the pronoun "it" must bind to "trophy". The pronoun's query q"it"q_{\text{"it"}}q"it"​ specifically searches for physical dimensions in preceding noun keys, matching the key k"trophy"k_{\text{"trophy"}}k"trophy"​ (which advertises physical bulk), allowing "it" to absorb the semantic properties of the trophy rather than the suitcase.
Figure 2.1: Scaled Dot-Product Attention Engine — Projections, Compatibility Matrix, Scaling, Softmax & Value Blending

2.2 Raw Compatibility Scoring (QKTQ K^TQKT)

💡 Why?

  • Dynamic Content-Based Routing: To route information adaptively across a sequence, the model must measure pairwise relevance between all tokens dynamically rather than using static topological distance.
  • Architectural Role: The matrix product S=QKTS = Q K^TS=QKT calculates the unscaled dot-product similarity (raw affinity logits) between every query vector qiq_iqi​ and every key vector kjk_jkj​, yielding an N×NN \times NN×N dense connectivity matrix.
  • Failure Mode Without Dot-Product Affinity: Without an inner-product compatibility metric, the network would require either feed-forward additive networks for every pair (Bahdanau attention, which has an O(N2d)O(N^2 d)O(N2d) parameter and memory footprint that does not vectorize into high-throughput tensor cores) or fixed graph adjacencies. Removing pairwise scoring collapses the model into position-invariant pooling where tokens cannot selectively attend to specific syntactic dependencies.

📖 Definition & Architecture

In inner-product spaces, the dot product between two unit-normalized vectors represents the cosine of the angle between them; for unnormalized vectors, it scales with both directional alignment and magnitude. When query vector qiq_iqi​ is multiplied by key vector kjTk_j^TkjT​, the scalar output si,j=⟨qi,kj⟩=∑m=1dkqi,mkj,ms_{i,j} = \langle q_i, k_j \rangle = \sum_{m=1}^{d_k} q_{i,m} k_{j,m}si,j​=⟨qi​,kj​⟩=∑m=1dk​​qi,m​kj,m​ serves as an unnormalized affinity metric.

When batched over the entire sequence of length NNN:

  • QQQ has dimensions N×dkN \times d_kN×dk​.
  • KTK^TKT has dimensions dk×Nd_k \times Ndk​×N.
  • The resulting matrix S=QKTS = Q K^TS=QKT has dimensions N×NN \times NN×N, where entry (i,j)(i, j)(i,j) represents the raw score of how strongly token iii attends to token jjj.

![Figure 2.2: Raw Compatibility Scoring Matrix Multiplication](assets/diagram_2_2_dot_product.jpg)

📐 The Mathematics & Working

The raw compatibility scoring operation is defined as:

Sraw=QKTS_{\text{raw}} = Q K^TSraw​=QKT

Or element-wise for any sequence pair (i,j)(i, j)(i,j):

si,j=qikjT=∑m=1dkqi,mkj,ms_{i,j} = q_i k_j^T = \sum_{m=1}^{d_k} q_{i,m} k_{j,m}si,j​=qi​kjT​=m=1∑dk​​qi,m​kj,m​
  • Q∈RN×dkQ \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_k}Q∈RN×dk​: Sequence query tensor containing NNN queries of dimension dkd_kdk​.
  • K∈RN×dkK \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_k}K∈RN×dk​: Sequence key tensor containing NNN keys of dimension dkd_kdk​.
  • KT∈Rdk×NK^T \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k \times N}KT∈Rdk​×N: Transposed key tensor.
  • Sraw∈RN×NS_{\text{raw}} \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times N}Sraw​∈RN×N: Square affinity matrix of raw, unnormalized compatibility scores (attention logits).
  • si,j∈Rs_{i,j} \in \mathbb{R}si,j​∈R: Scalar dot-product similarity score between query iii and key jjj.
  • dkd_kdk​: Hidden dimension of the key/query vector space.

2-Sentence Plain Lingo:

The model calculates the affinity between every pair of words by multiplying each word's query vector against every other word's key vector using matrix multiplication. The higher the resulting dot-product number, the more strongly the searching word believes the target word holds the context it requires.

🌍 Real-World & NLP Behaviors

  • Example 1: Prepositional Phrase Attachment: In the sentence "She saw the man with a telescope", the phrase "with a telescope" can modify "saw" (instrument of seeing) or "man" (holding a telescope). The dot product q"with"⋅k"saw"Tq_{\text{"with"}} \cdot k_{\text{"saw"}}^Tq"with"​⋅k"saw"T​ versus q"with"⋅k"man"Tq_{\text{"with"}} \cdot k_{\text{"man"}}^Tq"with"​⋅k"man"T​ determines which interpretation dominates based on semantic context learned in pre-training.
  • Example 2: Polysemy Disambiguation: For the ambiguous word "bank" in "He deposited money along the river bank", the query for "bank" computes positive dot products against both the financial key "deposited" and the geographical key "river"; whichever contextual signal produces a larger inner product pushes the representation toward its correct semantic cluster.

2.3 Variance Scaling Factor (1/dk1 / \sqrt{d_k}1/dk​​)

💡 Why?

  • Preventing Gradient Vanishing: As the projection dimension dkd_kdk​ grows large, the dot product between random independent zero-mean unit-variance vectors grows proportionally in variance (Var(q⋅k)=dk\text{Var}(q \cdot k) = d_kVar(q⋅k)=dk​), yielding large absolute magnitudes.
  • Architectural Role: Dividing the raw logits by dk\sqrt{d_k}dk​​ stabilizes the variance of the dot products back to 1.01.01.0, keeping the input to the subsequent softmax function within regions with non-zero gradients.

    • Failure Mode Without Scaling: Without the 1/dk1/\sqrt{d_k}1/dk​​ factor, for typical LLM dimensions such as dk=128d_k = 128dk​=128, dot products easily reach magnitudes of ±30\pm 30±30 to ±50\pm 50±50. Feeding logits of this magnitude into the softmax function pushes it into extreme saturation, where the largest element receives an attention probability of 1.01.01.0 and all others 0.00.00.0, driving the softmax derivative to zero (∂softmax∂z→0\frac{\partial \text{softmax}}{\partial z} \to 0∂z∂softmax​→0) and halting backpropagation during training.

📖 Definition & Architecture

Vaswani et al. (2017) observed that while dot-product attention is faster and more space-efficient in practice than additive attention due to optimized matrix multiplication code (BLAS/GEMM), it underperforms for large values of dkd_kdk​ unless properly scaled.

Assuming the components of q∈Rdkq \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k}q∈Rdk​ and k∈Rdkk \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k}k∈Rdk​ are independent random variables with mean E[qm]=E[km]=0\mathbb{E}[q_m] = \mathbb{E}[k_m] = 0E[qm​]=E[km​]=0 and unit variance Var(qm)=Var(km)=1\text{Var}(q_m) = \text{Var}(k_m) = 1Var(qm​)=Var(km​)=1:

  • The expectation of their product is E[qmkm]=0\mathbb{E}[q_m k_m] = 0E[qm​km​]=0.
  • The variance of their product is Var(qmkm)=E[qm2km2]−(E[qmkm])2=1⋅1−0=1\text{Var}(q_m k_m) = \mathbb{E}[q_m^2 k_m^2] - (\mathbb{E}[q_m k_m])^2 = 1 \cdot 1 - 0 = 1Var(qm​km​)=E[qm2​km2​]−(E[qm​km​])2=1⋅1−0=1.
  • The dot product q⋅k=∑m=1dkqmkmq \cdot k = \sum_{m=1}^{d_k} q_m k_mq⋅k=∑m=1dk​​qm​km​ is the sum of dkd_kdk​ independent random variables, giving E[q⋅k]=0\mathbb{E}[q \cdot k] = 0E[q⋅k]=0 and Var(q⋅k)=∑m=1dk1=dk\text{Var}(q \cdot k) = \sum_{m=1}^{d_k} 1 = d_kVar(q⋅k)=∑m=1dk​​1=dk​.
  • The standard deviation is therefore σ=dk\sigma = \sqrt{d_k}σ=dk​​.

    Scaling by τ=1dk\tau = \frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}}τ=dk​​1​ renormalizes the variance: Var(q⋅kdk)=1dkVar(q⋅k)=dkdk=1.0\text{Var}\left(\frac{q \cdot k}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) = \frac{1}{d_k} \text{Var}(q \cdot k) = \frac{d_k}{d_k} = 1.0Var(dk​​q⋅k​)=dk​1​Var(q⋅k)=dk​dk​​=1.0.

    ![Figure 2.3: Variance Scaling Factor 1/sqrt(d_k) and Gradient Active Region](assets/diagram_2_3_scaling.jpg)

📐 The Mathematics & Working

The scaled logit matrix SSS is expressed as:

S=QKTdkS = \frac{Q K^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}S=dk​​QKT​

Element-wise:

si,j=∑m=1dkqi,mkj,mdks_{i,j} = \frac{\sum_{m=1}^{d_k} q_{i,m} k_{j,m}}{\sqrt{d_k}}si,j​=dk​​∑m=1dk​​qi,m​kj,m​​

Under the statistical assumption:

qi,m,kj,m∼i.i.d. N(0,1)  ⟹  E[si,j]=0,Var(si,j)=1q_{i,m}, k_{j,m} \sim \text{i.i.d. } \mathcal{N}(0, 1) \implies \mathbb{E}[s_{i,j}] = 0, \quad \text{Var}(s_{i,j}) = 1qi,m​,kj,m​∼i.i.d. N(0,1)⟹E[si,j​]=0,Var(si,j​)=1
  • S∈RN×NS \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times N}S∈RN×N: Scaled affinity matrix of attention logits.
  • Q∈RN×dkQ \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_k}Q∈RN×dk​: Query matrix.
  • KT∈Rdk×NK^T \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k \times N}KT∈Rdk​×N: Transposed key matrix.
  • dkd_kdk​: Dimensionality of the key projection subspace per head.
  • dk\sqrt{d_k}dk​​: The square root of the head dimension acting as a variance temperature divisor.

    2-Sentence Plain Lingo:

    Multiplying high-dimensional vectors adds up dozens of numbers, causing the total score to blow up to extreme values that would freeze the model's learning process. Dividing the result by the square root of the vector length shrinks the numbers back into a safe range where gradients can flow freely.

🌍 Real-World & NLP Behaviors

  • Example 1: Initial Training Convergence of Large LLMs: In early pretraining iterations of models like LLaMA-3 (dk=128d_k = 128dk​=128), omitting dk\sqrt{d_k}dk​​ results in immediate loss spikes and gradient underflow within the first 100 optimizer steps, because unscaled initial logits push softmax outputs to exact 000 and 111 floating-point limits.

    • Example 2: Multi-Token Soft Focus in Machine Translation: When translating an idiomatic phrase like "kick the bucket" into another language, the model must distribute attention across all three words concurrently. The variance scaling factor prevents the attention from collapsing onto a single token (e.g., exclusively "bucket"), allowing the model to blend the combined semantic meaning of the entire idiom.

2.4 Softmax Normalization

💡 Why?

  • Probabilistic Convex Combination: Raw scaled affinity scores are unbounded real values (−∞-\infty−∞ to +∞+\infty+∞). To construct a valid convex combination of value vectors, attention scores must form a strict probability simplex across keys for each query.
  • Architectural Role: Applying row-wise softmax normalizes the affinity scores such that ∑j=1NAi,j=1.0\sum_{j=1}^N A_{i,j} = 1.0∑j=1N​Ai,j​=1.0 and Ai,j≥0A_{i,j} \ge 0Ai,j​≥0 for all i,ji, ji,j.
  • Failure Mode Without Softmax: If unnormalized scores were used, sequence outputs would fluctuate wildly in magnitude depending on sequence length NNN and token activation norms, leading to exploding or vanishing residual stream activations. Sigmoid normalization fails because it allows all tokens to be simultaneously ignored or saturated without forcing a competitive trade-off across context positions.

📖 Definition & Architecture

The softmax function exponentiates each scaled logit and divides it by the sum of exponentiated logits across the key dimension (row-wise across the columns of the N×NN \times NN×N matrix).

For numerical stability in hardware implementations (avoiding floating-point overflow when computing esi,je^{s_{i,j}}esi,j​), modern runtime kernels (such as FlashAttention by Dao et al., 2022) utilize the mathematically equivalent online safe softmax:

mi=max⁡j(si,j),softmax(si)j=exp⁡(si,j−mi)∑l=1Nexp⁡(si,l−mi)m_i = \max_j (s_{i,j}), \quad \text{softmax}(s_i)_j = \frac{\exp(s_{i,j} - m_i)}{\sum_{l=1}^N \exp(s_{i,l} - m_i)}mi​=jmax​(si,j​),softmax(si​)j​=∑l=1N​exp(si,l​−mi​)exp(si,j​−mi​)​

This guarantees that the maximum exponent is exp⁡(0)=1\exp(0) = 1exp(0)=1, preventing IEEE 754 float16/bfloat16 overflow while preserving exact probability ratios.

![Figure 2.4: Softmax Row-wise Probability Normalization](assets/diagram_2_4_softmax.jpg)

📐 The Mathematics & Working

The attention weight matrix A∈RN×NA \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times N}A∈RN×N is formulated as:

A=softmax(QKTdk)A = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)A=softmax(dk​​QKT​)

Element-wise for row iii and column jjj:

Ai,j=exp⁡(qikjTdk)∑l=1Nexp⁡(qiklTdk)A_{i,j} = \frac{\exp\left(\frac{q_i k_j^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)}{\sum_{l=1}^N \exp\left(\frac{q_i k_l^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)}Ai,j​=∑l=1N​exp(dk​​qi​klT​​)exp(dk​​qi​kjT​​)​

Subject to the probability simplex constraints:

∀i,j:0≤Ai,j≤1,and∑j=1NAi,j=1.0\forall i, j: \quad 0 \le A_{i,j} \le 1, \quad \text{and} \quad \sum_{j=1}^N A_{i,j} = 1.0∀i,j:0≤Ai,j​≤1,andj=1∑N​Ai,j​=1.0
  • A∈RN×NA \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times N}A∈RN×N: The row-stochastic attention weight matrix (each row forms a probability distribution).
  • Ai,jA_{i,j}Ai,j​: The scalar probability mass allocated by token iii to token jjj.
  • qi∈Rdkq_i \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k}qi​∈Rdk​: Query vector of token iii.
  • kj∈Rdkk_j \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k}kj​∈Rdk​: Key vector of token jjj.
  • NNN: Sequence length (number of tokens in the context window).

2-Sentence Plain Lingo:

The softmax operation turns arbitrary compatibility numbers into a percentage-based budget that sums up to exactly one hundred percent for each word. This forces the model to make trade-offs by deciding exactly what fraction of its attention budget to allocate to each word in the sentence.

🌍 Real-World & NLP Behaviors

  • Example 1: Long-Context Distraction / Needle-in-a-Haystack: In a 32,000-token context window, if many irrelevant tokens have slightly positive dot products, the softmax denominator accumulates a large sum ∑exp⁡(s)\sum \exp(s)∑exp(s), which can dilute the probability weight assigned to a single relevant "needle" fact down from 0.950.950.95 to 0.050.050.05.
  • Example 2: Syntactic Tree Induction in Transformer Heads: Probing studies (e.g., Clark et al., 2019, What Does BERT Look At?) show that specific attention heads use the softmax distribution to simulate discrete syntactic dependency pointers: a head specialized for direct objects will place over 90%90\%90% of its softmax probability mass on the noun governed by a transitive verb.

2.5 Weighted Value Aggregation

💡 Why?

  • Synthesizing Context-Enriched Representations: Attention scores alone are merely routing weights; they carry no semantic content. The network must physically extract and mix token features to produce updated representations.
  • Architectural Role: The final stage of scaled dot-product attention computes the matrix product Z=AVZ = A VZ=AV, which takes a linear combination of all value vectors vjv_jvj​ weighted by their attention probabilities Ai,jA_{i,j}Ai,j​.
  • Failure Mode Without Value Aggregation: If an architecture directly returned the attention matrix AAA or summed queries and keys, it would only have access to relational connectivity graphs without an updated contextualized embedding. Without weighted value aggregation, token vectors remain frozen in their static, context-free initial states.

📖 Definition & Architecture

Vaswani et al. (2017) complete the scaled dot-product attention equation with the value multiplication:

Attention(Q,K,V)=softmax(QKTdk)V=AV\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) V = A VAttention(Q,K,V)=softmax(dk​​QKT​)V=AV

For any given token iii, its output vector ziz_izi​ is a barycentric point (convex combination) inside the convex hull spanned by the set of all value vectors {v1,v2,…,vN}\{v_1, v_2, \dots, v_N\}{v1​,v2​,…,vN​}.

If token iii attends 90%90\%90% to token jjj and 10%10\%10% to token kkk, the resulting representation ziz_izi​ is composed of 0.90vj+0.10vk0.90 v_j + 0.10 v_k0.90vj​+0.10vk​. This contextual representation is subsequently passed to the multi-head projection or residual add-and-norm pipeline.

![Figure 2.5: Weighted Value Aggregation and Output Representation](assets/diagram_2_5_value_aggregation.jpg)

📐 The Mathematics & Working

The weighted aggregation is computed by matrix multiplication:

Z=AV=softmax(QKTdk)VZ = A V = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) VZ=AV=softmax(dk​​QKT​)V

Or vectorially for each token position iii:

zi=∑j=1NAi,jvjz_i = \sum_{j=1}^N A_{i,j} v_jzi​=j=1∑N​Ai,j​vj​
  • A∈RN×NA \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times N}A∈RN×N: Normalized attention probability matrix (∑jAi,j=1\sum_j A_{i,j} = 1∑j​Ai,j​=1).
  • V∈RN×dvV \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_v}V∈RN×dv​: Value matrix, where row jjj is the value vector vj∈Rdvv_j \in \mathbb{R}^{d_v}vj​∈Rdv​.
  • Z∈RN×dvZ \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_v}Z∈RN×dv​: Output matrix of contextualized token representations, where row iii is zi∈Rdvz_i \in \mathbb{R}^{d_v}zi​∈Rdv​.
  • Ai,jA_{i,j}Ai,j​: The scalar attention weight of token iii on token jjj.
  • vjv_jvj​: The value representation of token jjj.
  • ziz_izi​: The context-aggregated output vector for position iii.

2-Sentence Plain Lingo:

The model uses the percentage scores from the softmax step to mix together the actual content payloads of every word in the sentence. Each word ends up with a newly updated meaning built from a custom recipe of information collected across the entire text.

🌍 Real-World & NLP Behaviors

  • Example 1: Contextual Word Sense Specialization: In "Apple released the new M4 MacBook Pro", the initial embedding for "Apple" contains features of both a fruit and a corporation. Through value aggregation, "Apple" places high attention weight on "MacBook" and "released", pulling their value vectors into its own representation and shifting its residual state toward technology and commerce.
  • Example 2: Cross-Lingual Feature Alignment: In neural machine translation models, a target token attending across the encoder's source sequence aggregates value vectors from the foreign language sentence, pulling grammatical gender, tense, and number directly into the decoder's next-token predictive state.

Module 3: Multi-Head & Causal Decoding

While single scaled dot-product attention can route information across sequence positions, a single head is limited to computing an average across a single distribution, preventing simultaneous tracking of different semantic phenomena. Furthermore, generative language modeling requires that representations strictly respect temporal causality. In this module, we dissect the mechanics of multi-head subspace splitting, output recombining, causal autoregressive masking, and the stateful KV-cache acceleration mechanism.

3.1 Multi-Head Subspace Splitting (hhh Parallel Heads)

💡 Why?

  • Multiple Simultaneous Interaction Channels: In language, tokens interact across multiple orthogonal linguistic levels at the exact same time (e.g., syntactic dependency, semantic coreference, factual associations, and rhythmic or positional cadence). A single attention head can only construct one probability distribution per token, forcing an undesirable averaging across competing dependencies.
  • Architectural Role: Multi-Head Attention linearly projects queries, keys, and values hhh times with different learned parameter matrices into lower-dimensional subspaces (dk=dmodel/hd_k = d_{\text{model}} / hdk​=dmodel​/h). Each head independently computes scaled dot-product attention in parallel, enabling the network to focus on information from different representation subspaces at different positions.
  • Failure Mode Without Multi-Head Splitting: If a model uses a single full-dimensional attention head with dimension dmodeld_{\text{model}}dmodel​, its attention weights average out all contextual influences into a single blurred centroid. The model cannot simultaneously track who did what to whom (subject-verb-object) while resolving pronoun antecedents, causing an immediate drop in grammatical precision and compositionality.

📖 Definition & Architecture

Vaswani et al. (2017) defined Multi-Head Attention as running hhh attention heads in parallel. Rather than performing a single attention function with dmodeld_{\text{model}}dmodel​-dimensional queries, keys, and values, the model projects the queries, keys, and values hhh times with separate, learned linear projections to dk,dk,d_k, d_k,dk​,dk​, and dvd_vdv​ dimensions respectively:

headi=Attention(QWiQ,KWiK,VWiV)\text{head}_i = \text{Attention}(Q W_i^Q, K W_i^K, V W_i^V)headi​=Attention(QWiQ​,KWiK​,VWiV​)

Where each head operates on vectors of reduced dimension dk=dv=dmodel/hd_k = d_v = d_{\text{model}} / hdk​=dv​=dmodel​/h. This ensures that the total computational cost of multi-head attention is identical to single-head attention with full dimensionality dmodeld_{\text{model}}dmodel​, while multiplying the model's expressive representational bandwidth by hhh.

![Figure 3.1: Multi-Head Attention Subspace Splitting](assets/diagram_3_1_multihead.jpg)

📐 The Mathematics & Working

The multi-head attention splitting is formalized as:

MultiHead(Q,K,V)=Concat(head1,head2,…,headh)WO\text{MultiHead}(Q, K, V) = \text{Concat}(\text{head}_1, \text{head}_2, \dots, \text{head}_h) W^OMultiHead(Q,K,V)=Concat(head1​,head2​,…,headh​)WO

Where each individual head is computed as:

headi=Attention(XWiQ,XWiK,XWiV)=softmax((XWiQ)(XWiK)Tdk)(XWiV)\text{head}_i = \text{Attention}(X W_i^Q, X W_i^K, X W_i^V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{(X W_i^Q)(X W_i^K)^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) (X W_i^V)headi​=Attention(XWiQ​,XWiK​,XWiV​)=softmax(dk​​(XWiQ​)(XWiK​)T​)(XWiV​)

  • X∈RN×dmodelX \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_{\text{model}}}X∈RN×dmodel​: Input sequence tensor.
  • hhh: Number of parallel attention heads (e.g., h=32h = 32h=32 in LLaMA-7B, h=64h = 64h=64 in LLaMA-70B).
  • dmodeld_{\text{model}}dmodel​: Dimensionality of the model's main residual stream.
  • dk=dmodel/hd_k = d_{\text{model}} / hdk​=dmodel​/h: Subspace dimensionality per attention head.
  • WiQ∈Rdmodel×dkW_i^Q \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}WiQ​∈Rdmodel​×dk​: Query projection matrix for head iii.
  • WiK∈Rdmodel×dkW_i^K \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}WiK​∈Rdmodel​×dk​: Key projection matrix for head iii.
  • WiV∈Rdmodel×dvW_i^V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_v}WiV​∈Rdmodel​×dv​: Value projection matrix for head iii.
  • headi∈RN×dv\text{head}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_v}headi​∈RN×dv​: The output tensor of the iii-th attention head.

2-Sentence Plain Lingo:

Instead of having one single observer analyze the entire sentence, the model divides its thinking space into multiple parallel experts who each look at the sentence through different lenses. One expert can track who is performing the action, while another simultaneously monitors when and where the action takes place.

🌍 Real-World & NLP Behaviors

  • Example 1: Specialized Syntactic and Positional Induction: In empirical attention analysis of GPT-class architectures, Head 1 in Layer 3 consistently acts as a "previous-token head" (attending strictly to position i−1i-1i−1), while Head 7 in the same layer tracks punctuation boundaries, and Head 12 specializes in tracking syntactic parent-child dependencies.
  • Example 2: Multi-Hop Question Answering: When answering "Where was the author of 'Hamlet' born?", one attention head binds "author of 'Hamlet'" to "William Shakespeare", while a parallel attention head simultaneously tracks the location query linking "born" to "Stratford-upon-Avon".

3.2 Output Linear Projection (WOW_OWO​)

💡 Why?

  • Subspace Integration and Dimensional Re-alignment: The raw output of multi-head attention is a simple concatenation of hhh separate low-dimensional head vectors. The model needs a parameterized mechanism to synthesize, mix, and reconcile the parallel observations made by each head before reinjecting them into the main residual stream.
  • Architectural Role: The output projection matrix WO∈Rdmodel×dmodelW^O \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_{\text{model}}}WO∈Rdmodel​×dmodel​ linearly projects the concatenated head outputs back into the residual stream space, allowing cross-head communication and feature blending.
  • Failure Mode Without Output Projection: Concatenation without projection leaves the heads partitioned in isolated coordinate slices without cross-head feature interaction. Furthermore, if head dimensions do not sum to dmodeld_{\text{model}}dmodel​ (or in architectures with asymmetric value dimensions), the output cannot be added back into the residual stream via identity skip connections (X+MHA(X)X + \text{MHA}(X)X+MHA(X)).

📖 Definition & Architecture

After each of the hhh heads produces its output tensor headi∈RN×dv\text{head}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_v}headi​∈RN×dv​, the vectors are concatenated along the feature dimension to form a composite tensor:

Hconcat=[head1 ∥ head2 ∥ … ∥ headh]∈RN×(h⋅dv)H_{\text{concat}} = [\text{head}_1 \,\|\, \text{head}_2 \,\|\, \dots \,\|\, \text{head}_h] \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times (h \cdot d_v)}Hconcat​=[head1​∥head2​∥…∥headh​]∈RN×(h⋅dv​)

Assuming h⋅dv=dmodelh \cdot d_v = d_{\text{model}}h⋅dv​=dmodel​, this concatenated matrix has shape N×dmodelN \times d_{\text{model}}N×dmodel​.

The linear transformation WO∈Rdmodel×dmodelW^O \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_{\text{model}}}WO∈Rdmodel​×dmodel​ is applied as a matrix multiplication:

Zout=HconcatWOZ_{\text{out}} = H_{\text{concat}} W^OZout​=Hconcat​WO

This operation can be interpreted as a set of linear combinations that blend features discovered in Head AAA with features discovered in Head BBB, producing a unified, coherent update vector suitable for addition to the residual stream.

![Figure 3.2: Multi-Head Concatenation and Output Projection W_O](assets/diagram_3_2_output_proj.jpg)

📐 The Mathematics & Working

The output linear projection is expressed as:

Zout=(⨁i=1hheadi)WO=[head1 ∥ head2 ∥ … ∥ headh]WOZ_{\text{out}} = \left( \bigoplus_{i=1}^h \text{head}_i \right) W^O = [\text{head}_1 \,\|\, \text{head}_2 \,\|\, \dots \,\|\, \text{head}_h] W^OZout​=(i=1⨁h​headi​)WO=[head1​∥head2​∥…∥headh​]WO

Equivalently, expressing WOW^OWO as hhh partitioned submatrices WO=[W1OW2O⋮WhO]W^O = \begin{bmatrix} W_1^O \\ W_2^O \\ \vdots \\ W_h^O \end{bmatrix}WO=​W1O​W2O​⋮WhO​​​ where each WiO∈Rdv×dmodelW_i^O \in \mathbb{R}^{d_v \times d_{\text{model}}}WiO​∈Rdv​×dmodel​:

Zout=∑i=1hheadiWiOZ_{\text{out}} = \sum_{i=1}^h \text{head}_i W_i^OZout​=i=1∑h​headi​WiO​
  • headi∈RN×dv\text{head}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_v}headi​∈RN×dv​: Output activation tensor from the iii-th attention head.
  • ∥\|∥ or ⨁\bigoplus⨁: Concatenation along the feature (channel) dimension.
  • WO∈R(h⋅dv)×dmodelW^O \in \mathbb{R}^{(h \cdot d_v) \times d_{\text{model}}}WO∈R(h⋅dv​)×dmodel​: Output linear projection weight parameter tensor.
  • WiO∈Rdv×dmodelW_i^O \in \mathbb{R}^{d_v \times d_{\text{model}}}WiO​∈Rdv​×dmodel​: The specific slice of WOW^OWO acting on the iii-th head.
  • Zout∈RN×dmodelZ_{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_{\text{model}}}Zout​∈RN×dmodel​: Recombined multi-head output matrix matched to the residual stream dimensionality.

2-Sentence Plain Lingo:

Once all the separate attention heads finish their individual analyses, their answers are lined up side by side and passed through a final mixing matrix. This step synthesizes all their separate observations into a single unified summary that fits directly back into the main network highway.

🌍 Real-World & NLP Behaviors

  • Example 1: Cross-Head Feature Cancellation and Conflict Resolution: When Head 2 flags a token as a potential noun and Head 5 flags it as a participle adjective, WOW^OWO contains learned negative and positive cross-terms that reconcile the ambiguity before the representation enters the Feed-Forward Layer (FFN).
  • Example 2: Residual Stream Alignment in Instruction Tuning: In residual-stream interpretability studies (e.g., Elhage et al., 2021, A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits), WOW^OWO is shown to write specific directional updates into the residual stream that directly activate down-stream MLP neurons corresponding to instruction execution.

3.3 Causal Triangular Attention Masking

💡 Why?

  • Preserving Autoregressive Causality: Autoregressive language models generate text sequentially from left to right. The probability of the next token xt+1x_{t+1}xt+1​ must depend strictly on the historical context x≤tx_{\le t}x≤t​ and cannot condition on future tokens x>tx_{> t}x>t​.
  • Architectural Role: In parallel training mode, where the entire ground-truth sequence is fed into the model simultaneously, causal masking applies an additive mask MMM to the attention logits prior to softmax, setting all upper-triangular entries (future positions) to −∞-\infty−∞.
  • Failure Mode Without Causal Masking: Without the causal mask, token xtx_txt​ can attend directly to token xt+1x_{t+1}xt+1​ during training. This creates trivial information leakage ("cheating"), causing training loss to collapse to near zero while rendering the model completely incapable of generating text autoregressively at inference time.

📖 Definition & Architecture

During training, Transformers process all NNN tokens in parallel using matrix multiplication. To maintain the autoregressive property P(x1,…,xN)=∏t=1NP(xt∣x<t)P(x_1, \dots, x_N) = \prod_{t=1}^N P(x_t \mid x_{<t})P(x1​,…,xN​)=∏t=1N​P(xt​∣x<t​), the attention matrix must be strictly lower triangular.

The causal mask matrix M∈RN×NM \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times N}M∈RN×N is defined as:

Mi,j={0if j≤i−∞if j>iM_{i,j} = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } j \le i \\ -\infty & \text{if } j > i \end{cases}Mi,j​={0−∞​if j≤iif j>i​

When added to the scaled affinity matrix S=QKTdkS = \frac{Q K^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}S=dk​​QKT​, any position with −∞-\infty−∞ evaluates to exactly zero under the softmax exponential:

exp⁡(−∞)=0\exp(-\infty) = 0exp(−∞)=0

Consequently, token iii assigns zero probability mass to any token at index j>ij > ij>i.
